summary.intent: Build a full interactive TUI dashboard for the memory-loop system using Charmbracelet/bubbletea libraries, replacing plain text output with a tab-based interface for browsing, managing, and configuring memory records.
summary.outcome: A bubbletea TUI was scaffolded and iteratively improved across multiple fix cycles. Core structure with 4 tabs (Memories, Injection, History, Settings) was built, but the session ended mid-fix with ongoing issues around border visibility, settings key handling, and injection tab overflow.

repo: The project uses a `termstyle` package for ANSI 256 colors with NO_COLOR support — new TUI components should integrate with this rather than using raw lipgloss colors directly.
ACCESSIBLE=1 env var is used as a feature flag to fall back to plain-text output for screen readers; the TUI respects this by skipping bubbletea and delegating to existing show/status subcommands.
Memory loop state lives in `.entire/memory-loop.json`; the TUI requires `entire memory-loop refresh` to have been run first to have data.

The project uses `memoryloop.TransitionRecordLifecycle`, `memoryloop.SelectRelevant`, `memoryloop.AddManualRecord`, `memoryloop.PruneRecords`, and `memoryloop.SaveState` as the core API for mutations.
The docs/superpowers directory is gitignored — brainstorm artifacts and specs written there won't appear in git history.

code.finding: Border color '8' (dark gray) is invisible on dark terminals; use '245' (light gray) instead. Accent color was changed from cyan ('6') to orange ('214') per user preference.

Lipgloss bordered card width must be set to `width - 2` unconditionally (not conditionally on width > 0) to ensure it always renders. Detail pane should default to shown (showDetail: true) rather than requiring an Enter keypress.

Settings key handling was unreliable when using tea.Cmd closures with pointer fields for settingsChangedMsg. Switching to synchronous inline state mutations (no tea.Cmd) was more reliable for simple toggle operations.

Log table height calculated as `h - 10` was insufficient when detail card (~10 lines) + prompt tester (~3 lines) + labels (~3 lines) are all present, causing content to overflow and push the tab bar off-screen.

Key delegation in the root model's Update function: after global key handling, the remaining msg is passed to active tab — but the typed tea.KeyMsg from the type switch must be correctly forwarded, not the original untyped tea.Msg.

workflow: The brainstorming skill's visual companion (local HTTP server) is effective for getting user approval on layout/design decisions before writing code — interactive HTML mockups let users click to select preferences.

Subagent-driven development works well for sequential implementation tasks but requires explicit commit discipline — subagents may complete work without committing, leaving changes that appear as uncommitted diffs.

Iterative screenshot-driven feedback cycles (user shares screenshots, assistant diagnoses diffs from mockup) are effective but slow; many small fix commits accumulated rather than one clean implementation.
For bubbletea TUIs, test with an actual terminal early — lipgloss styling issues (border colors, width calculations) are not detectable from code review alone and require visual verification.
The writing-plans + subagent-driven-development skill combination provides a structured workflow: brainstorm → spec → plan → implement → review, with each phase gating the next.

friction: Lipgloss border color '8' (dark gray) was invisibly dark on the user's terminal — this caused multiple rounds of 'borders not showing' feedback before the root cause (color value too dark) was identified.
The maxWidth=80 cap made the layout feel cramped on a wider terminal; this required an explicit fix pass.
Settings tab key handling required multiple fix attempts — the tea.Cmd closure approach didn't work reliably, requiring a switch to synchronous mutations.
Injection tab content overflow (tab bar pushed off-screen) required careful height arithmetic that wasn't obvious from the initial implementation.
The brainstorm visual companion server shuts down between sessions and must be manually restarted with content re-written.
The docs/superpowers gitignore meant design artifacts (spec, plan HTML mockups) couldn't be committed alongside the code, reducing traceability.
Multiple subagent dispatches for fix cycles added latency and created fragmented commit history rather than clean logical commits.
open_items: Settings tab key handling and visual design were still being fixed at session end — final state unknown.
Injection tab overflow fix was applied but not verified in a screenshot.
History tab 'R' refresh trigger is a placeholder — async refresh wiring to the actual memoryloop.Refresh function is not implemented.
Unit tests for the TUI package are explicitly deferred — the design spec noted 'manual verification' focus only.
The Add Memory form (Task 8) was implemented but not visually verified against the mockup.
lipgloss v1 API compatibility should be verified — context7 docs were consulted mid-session suggesting potential API differences.
Injection prompt tester scoring/matching logic needs end-to-end verification that SelectRelevant is actually being called correctly with the input prompt.
